desc: The Navy squadron that flew the 14 November 2004 intercept. Commanded by David Fravor and embarked in USS Nimitz with Carrier Air Wing Eleven, VFA-41 put two F/A-18F sections into the encounter: Fravor and Alex Dietrich on the visual intercept, and a follow-on aircraft whose ATFLIR pod produced the footage released fourteen years later as FLIR1. The squadron is the point where the institutional failure is easiest to see. Fravor testified that 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken' - meaning that the Navy neither debriefed nor collected from the aircrew who had just intercepted an unidentified 46-foot object inside a working range, but the event nonetheless generated a classified range fouler report that died at Third Fleet. Twenty years later the same squadron's aircrew are the two named witnesses in the FOIA-released Navy documentation of the incident, and the video their aircraft produced is one of three the Department of Defense has ever officially acknowledged.
